note: Modern museum interpretation written to accompany the Chicago History Museum's pictures of the pre-fire city, each caption naming its picture (ichi- numbers). Used for the Last Sunday jaunt's places: what each building was, who built it and what it held on 8 October 1871. Where it disagrees with Andreas (the Palmer House: it puts the hotel standing at the fire on the southeast corner of State and Monroe, opened in March 1871; Andreas puts it at the northwest corner of State and Quincy, opened 26 September 1870), the jaunt says only what both agree on.
what_it_supplies: the Court House's block, cupola, watchman's balcony 120 feet up, clock and 10,849-pound bell
the Sherman House's Athens marble, its Clark Street portico, and William Gallagher's letter placing Theodore Thomas there
the Chamber of Commerce's dedication on 30 August 1865 and its commodities exchange
Crosby's Opera House: its front, shops, 3,000 seats, summer renovation and the Thomas reopening set for 9 October
Potter Palmer's State Street, the Field & Leiter store and the Palmer House
the Water Tower and Pumping Station, the lake tunnel and crib
the Saturday Night Fire of 7-8 October and the O'Leary cottage and barn
what_it_does_not_supply: measured dimensions or surveyed positions for any building
who was on any street on the afternoon of 8 October
